paths.description: Anonymous entry/login and consent experience; primary logged-out archetype.
Public profile/detail archetype represented by Instagram’s own profile, including no-JS crawler comparison.
Account creation form archetype; inspected without submitting personal data.
Account recovery form and recovery-state archetype; inspected without submitting identifiers.

findings.summary: A consent interstitial obscures the entire primary surface on every anonymous path.
findings.evidence: Desktop, mobile, signup, reset, and profile screenshots all show a full-modal cookie prompt before users can use the page; on 360x800 its long explanatory copy consumes almost the whole viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Use the least intrusive consent surface permitted, minimise first-layer copy, preserve equal prominence for accept/decline, and keep core page context visible.

findings.summary: The consent modal is a custom ARIA dialog rather than a native dialog primitive.
findings.evidence: DOM probe found zero <dialog> elements and one role=dialog custom div; Lighthouse also found that custom dialog has no accessible name.
findings.suggestedFix: Use <dialog> with showModal(), aria-labelledby, platform focus management, and an explicit close/choice path.

findings.summary: Anonymous route changes are abrupt and do not preserve visual continuity.
findings.evidence: The route-transition video records navigation from login toward password recovery with no authored View Transition; the page probe found no active animations.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a conservative same-document or cross-document View Transition for authentication-route changes and disable it under reduced motion.

findings.summary: Authentication-route changes provide no visual attention cue.
findings.evidence: The route-transition video shows an immediate route replacement with the modal remaining dominant, rather than a directional cue that establishes where context moved.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a reduced-motion-safe directional transition and move focus to the new page heading.

findings.summary: Largest Contentful Paint is far outside the good range.
findings.evidence: Trace measured LCP 9.21s and Lighthouse measured 13.2s, performance 0.58, TTI 18.2s and TBT 300ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the true LCP resource, reduce startup JavaScript, and defer non-critical consent/help modules.

findings.summary: The logged-out shell ships excessive, mostly unused JavaScript.
findings.evidence: HAR measured 2.83MB transferred with 1.73MB of script; Lighthouse estimated 1,616KiB unused JavaScript and 6.28s potential LCP savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Create a minimal logged-out/auth bundle and conditionally load feed, media, and account modules only when required.

findings.summary: The cookie dialog has no accessible name.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility 0.87 reports aria-dialog-name as a serious failure for the full-viewport role=dialog; the visible H2 is not connected with aria-labelledby.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the dialog an accessible name via native <dialog> plus aria-labelledby referencing its visible heading.

findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured Meta Products and Cookies Policy links at 1.31:1 (#00376b on #212328), below the required 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a lighter link token in dark mode that reaches at least 4.5:1, and verify in forced-colors mode.

findings.summary: Primary login controls do not expose a visible keyboard focus indicator.
findings.evidence: The focus probe focused the username, password, login, Facebook-login and several footer controls; computed outline was none and box-shadow none for the primary controls. Lighthouse also found skipped heading levels.
findings.suggestedFix: Use semantic buttons and :focus-visible with a high-contrast outline; repair the H2 to H4/H5 heading sequence.

findings.summary: The viewport caps user zoom below the accessibility baseline.
findings.evidence: DOM probe found maximum-scale=2, while Lighthouse mobile capture found maximum-scale=1 and failed meta-viewport; both prevent the 5x zoom expected by the audit.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale/minimum-scale restrictions and verify reflow at 200% and 400% zoom.

findings.summary: Deprecated unload handling blocks the back/forward cache.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found an unload listener in lc-ZCWMeITD.js, one deprecation warning, three BFCache blockers, and missing source maps for large first-party JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace unload with pagehide/visibilitychange where needed, remove avoidable no-store responses, and publish production source maps securely.

findings.summary: Public profile content is effectively absent without JavaScript and generic crawlers are blocked.
findings.evidence: Profile discoverability measured 1% raw/rendered word coverage, isJsShell=true and no raw title; robots.txt applies Disallow: / to User-agent * and separately blocks major AI crawlers.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render public profile identity and key post metadata; align robots policy with the audiences the site intends to reach.

findings.summary: The browser policy set is strong but has avoidable XSS/referrer gaps.
findings.evidence: Headers show HSTS, nosniff, DENY framing and Permissions-Policy, but CSP allows unsafe-inline styles/wasm unsafe eval and Referrer-Policy is absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Set an explicit strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter Referrer-Policy and continue removing unsafe CSP allowances using nonces/hashes.

findings.summary: The public profile is a JavaScript shell for non-JS clients.
findings.evidence: Discoverability found only 1% content overlap for /instagram/, 57 raw text characters versus 3,354 rendered, and a crawler screenshot that contains only the splash logo.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render meaningful profile content and links, then hydrate enhancements without making core content depend on JavaScript.

findings.summary: The anonymous entry page uses a disproportionate resource budget.
findings.evidence: HAR transferred 2.83MB, 2.72MB from CDN/third-party origins; Lighthouse measured 3.54MB and 1.62MB unused JavaScript for a login shell.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a logged-out page-weight budget, split bundles by surface, and defer decorative media and non-essential modules.

findings.summary: The login and consent shell has a large in-memory footprint.
findings.evidence: A baseline heap snapshot contained 737,734 nodes and 38.67MB self size; after the repeated modal interaction probe it contained 748,094 nodes and 39.36MB. This does not prove a leak, but is disproportionate for the visible shell.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce the logged-out component and bundle graph, virtualise hidden consent detail, and track heap/DOM budgets in regression tests.
